selection_rule: Select one performance lead and one cost-down challenger before M1A; do not call either a winner until measured marine gates close.

finalists.name: D3_PERFORMANCE_LEAD
why_selected: Porous freeze-dried BC architectures are the strongest literature-backed class for high oil uptake and compressibility.
Hydrophobic surface engineering directly addresses native BC water affinity and therefore the key oil-over-water selectivity problem.
Mechanical squeezing recovery has a strong literature precedent for engineered BC aerogels.
finalists.winner_condition: Must pass all M1A/M1B gates and remain economically defensible on cost_per_kg_recovered_oil.

finalists.name: D1_COST_DOWN_CHALLENGER
why_selected: best chance to preserve a genuinely low-cost emergency-response proposition
finalists.winner_condition: Can defeat D3 even at lower g/g if it passes hard gates and materially lowers cost_per_kg_recovered_oil while remaining fully retrievable.

nonfinalist_controls.name: D2_FREEZE_DRY_UNMODIFIED
nonfinalist_controls.reason: Separates pore-preservation benefit from hydrophobic-surface benefit.

nonfinalist_controls.name: COMMERCIAL_OIL_SORBENT_PAD
nonfinalist_controls.reason: Prevents the project from optimizing only against itself.

feedstock_status.rule: Do not nominate green or black tea as material winner from literature alone. Advance the feedstock that wins the matched Stage-0 production/material screen.
feedstock_status.fallback_for_external_proposal: Describe feedstock as bacterial cellulose produced by SCOBY fermentation; present tea identity as an upstream optimization variable, not the claimed innovation.

winner_decision.after_hard_gates: Use Pareto comparison rather than an arbitrary weighted score: minimize cost_per_kg_recovered_oil and energy_per_kg_recovered_oil while maximizing selectivity, recovered oil, integrity and retrieval.

external_validation_targets.organization: CEDRE — Centre of Documentation, Research and Experimentation on Accidental Water Pollution
external_validation_targets.ask: Independent advice/test design for sorbent pads and a 1 m retrievable BC boom cartridge under salinity/current/temperature conditions; later standardized/custom/deployment testing.
external_validation_targets.why: CEDRE explicitly evaluates spill-response sorbents/equipment and can test under realistic environmental conditions.

external_validation_targets.organization: State Key Laboratory of New Textile Materials and Advanced Processing Technology / Wuhan Textile University
external_validation_targets.ask: Materials-science feedback or collaboration on robust crosslinked/hydrophobic BC aerogel processing and compression recovery.
external_validation_targets.why: Corresponding-author expertise in mechanically robust BC aerogels for oil absorption.

external_validation_targets.organization: Chuiko Institute of Surface Chemistry, National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine
external_validation_targets.ask: Local collaboration on porous-sorbent characterization, surface chemistry, adsorption and environmentally compatible surface modification.
external_validation_targets.why: Official institute research includes porous sorbents, adsorption and hybrid-material surface chemistry.

janus_tranception.forward: BC_BRANCH -> 100x100_M1A_PAD -> SALTWATER_SELECTIVITY -> RETRIEVAL -> PRESS_RECOVERY -> COST_ACCOUNTING -> EXTERNAL_VALIDATION -> MARINE_WINNER
janus_tranception.promotion_rule: A proposal, publication or external interest cannot promote a branch; only measured gates and independent/replicated evidence can.

next_action: Finish Stage-0 matched feedstock/process screen; fabricate D3 and D1 100x100 mm pads from the winning feedstock; run M1A static freshwater vs artificial seawater with D2 and a commercial control; send external validation proposal in parallel without claiming field readiness.
